theory.overview: A Suffix Tree is a compressed trie of all suffixes of a string. It enables O(m) pattern matching for a query of length m, and can find the longest repeated substring, longest common substring between two strings, and many other string problems in linear time. Suffix Arrays are a space-efficient alternative that store sorted suffix indices. Together with LCP (Longest Common Prefix) arrays, they solve the same problems with lower constant factors.

keyConcepts.name: Suffix Tree Construction
keyConcepts.description: Ukkonen's algorithm builds suffix tree in O(n) time. Each suffix is a path from root to leaf. Edges labeled with substrings.

keyConcepts.name: Suffix Array
keyConcepts.description: Array of all suffixes sorted lexicographically. SA[i] = starting index of i-th smallest suffix. O(n log n) construction.

keyConcepts.name: LCP Array
keyConcepts.description: Longest Common Prefix array. LCP[i] = length of common prefix between suffixes at SA[i] and SA[i-1]. Enables linear time solutions.

keyConcepts.name: Applications
keyConcepts.description: Pattern matching, longest repeated substring, longest common substring, longest palindrome, DNA sequencing, plagiarism detection.

complexity.patternMatch: O(m) where m is pattern length

algorithmSteps.description: LCP array: [0,1,3,0,0,2]. Max LCP=3 gives longest repeated substring 'ana'.
Search 'ana': Binary search suffix array, find occurrences at indices 1 and 3.
Longest repeated substring: 'ana' with length 3 (found via max LCP).
Build suffix tree using Ukkonen's algorithm in O(n) time.
